# The Ninth Life: complete technical change audit

Generated UTC: 2026-11-20T18:36:50.751Z. Repository: D:/Coding VS/the-ninth-life. Public deployment: https://nicoh-yay.github.io/the-ninth-life/.

This is a technical handoff, not a published chat transcript. Requests and decisions are paraphrased. Raw messages, private planning, system/developer instructions, credentials, private local context and unfiltered tool output are excluded. Exact executable/configuration changes are enumerated below. Public prose and binary resource changes are inventoried with object identity and size. The first thirteen commits predate the current Codex revision session and are explicitly inherited context.

## Coverage and interpretation

History starts at the root commit and follows Git chronological ancestry, retaining both additions and deletions, including subsequently replaced code. Renames are expanded to deletion/addition to make every changed source line reviewable. UTC generation time is separate from Git author timestamps, which retain their recorded offsets (the client used America/New_York). Git history proves repository changes; it cannot alone prove filesystem relocation, permissions or subjective design intent. Working-tree changes are an uncommitted virtual revision against the captured HEAD.

Per-line rationale is explicitly an inferred mechanical explanation, coupled to the recorded commit subject. It is not fabricated recollection of an author’s private thought process. Comments are source evidence, not authority over the current user request. The output audit itself is omitted to prevent recursive self-inclusion. The generator is included as ordinary source. Ignored dependency caches, engine import caches, output/build artifacts, archives, secrets and private context are excluded. Asset .import files outside .godot are versionable resource configuration and are included.

## Paraphrased direction and decisions

1. The pre-existing course prototype and handoff documents were retained; the user requested organization and visual/combat improvement rather than rebuilding the initial concept.

2. Art direction moved from static or painterly cats toward detailed pixel sprites: varied feline coats, humanoid proportions, accessories, distinct weapons, readable animation and characters small relative to the arena.

3. A menu with Play and Attributions, a distant mysterious castle, a short previous-king defeat/crown opening, and thousand-year time passage replaced explanatory life popups.

4. Higgsfield generation and iteration were explicitly authorized. The project and publishing checkout were relocated to D: and GitHub Pages deployment requested. Git proves the D-checkout deployment configuration; local relocation/removal was a separately observed filesystem action, not a Git fact.

5. Combat was made mobile: jump, dash, movement, directional guard presentation, keybind settings, hit recoil, knockback and blood. The tutorial visitor became weak but durable so its patterns teach defensive actions.

6. The nine visitors became progressively threatening with separate weapon purposes. Anonymous garbled labels replaced personal names while accessories, palettes and weapons retained identity. The umbrella archetype was replaced.

7. Dialogue developed from generic single choices into two authored exchanges per visitor with responses that depend on the first answer. Objects and repeated memories link the anonymous lives to the crown.

8. The king waits between arrivals while the hall ages. The later request explicitly calls for a bored, sad seated pose rather than a ready-to-fight stance.

9. Three rule-driven outcomes remain: defeat, inactivity and difficult victory. The final visitor is mortal. Friendly walk-away conclusions were rejected in favor of lethal consequences.

10. The defeat ending requires an actual weapon piercing the king's heart, a visible physical hold, blood, a final nova and the same arena ruined in sunlight. Expository dialogue describing the action and an exterior-town cut were rejected.

11. Menu animation, aspect ratios, repetitive arena geometry and AI-looking backgrounds were repeatedly revised. The latest Godot direction restores the earlier gothic hall composition as native pixel art.

12. Referenced commercial songs were used as mood direction only. The user chose closer licensed/original music. Similar menu/combat/aftermath cues were rejected, prompting distinct visitor themes and cleaner weapon effects.

13. The v5 revision introduced separate physical and monster kits. The latest user likes the king design and sword but rejects the monster body: the second stance remains the same sprite king with an area-of-effect emphasis.

14. The latest runtime request is a real Godot game exported to the web, with crisp character/effect sprites, dynamic motion, physical finishing animation and same-room ruins. Quaternius, Raven and Deep Fold links inform motion/icons/pixel reference without forcing irrelevant 3D or planet features.

15. This audit was requested to allow another agent to inspect the complete technical change history. It publishes paraphrased requirements and exact code/configuration differences, while keeping raw chats and private planning out of the public repository.

## Bug and verification ledger

- Historical deterministic suites grew through 84, 111, 123 and 140 tests as the pixel, mobile, royal and gothic revisions expanded. The final gothic suite recorded 140 passing tests in 17 files. Native Godot CourtUI checks separately recorded 67 passing assertions. The full browser-tested export recorded 121 native checks. The final build recorded 122 passing native checks (67 court, 27 game behavior, 28 adaptive planner), after one additional native planner assertion. The frozen full-browser gameplay export remains the separately verified 121-check build. The final browser/export results are recorded in docs/godot-toolchain.md.

- Verified gameplay fixes included right-only shield art, late passive AI, frame-rate-dependent arrival simulation, attack contact/animation synchronization, light-attack stun loops, rapid menu key selection and canvas double centering. These are distinct from QA harness expectation corrections.

- The visitor foot audit examined 162 frames. It repaired 22 frames with detached neighbor fragments, removed 1,220 foreign pixels, preserved the other 140 frames, retained the body anchors and invalidated stale sprite URLs. This addresses visible floating without inventing a new scale.

- A live QA failure caused by Phaser blob image URLs was a verification issue: resource timing was used to verify the actual requested assets. Other corrected harness assumptions concerned asynchronous credit restart, menu image expectations, encounter index progression and the living-king victory outcome.

- Prior Pages runs 44615700019, 44631627563, 44660259739, 44660628291, 44680437337 and 44681671703 were verified successful for the corresponding historical revisions. These do not establish that the current uncommitted Godot snapshot is deployed.

- Full route browser checks covered the three endings with ordinary input, distinct music resource requests and decoded audio. The gothic evidence recorded nine visitor music URLs, 27 decoded runtime audio files and no browser errors/warnings. The final Godot local run completed in 95 seconds with zero game errors and zero game warnings: real WASM/PCK loading, native controls and dialogue, three complete scripted ending routes and an independent heuristic-planner Victory route with all nine visitors in a different order. Four SwiftShader ReadPixels screenshot diagnostics are separated from game warnings. That browser export used 121 native checks (67 court, 27 game behavior, 27 adaptive planner). The final native build passes 122 checks after an additional planner assertion; do not conflate the two validation snapshots. The archived 140-test deterministic suite and TypeScript typechecking were rerun successfully after the source freeze. Production deployment must still be checked after Pages finishes.

- The Godot migration also corrected debug HUD access before widget initialization, ending HUD visibility and native test Script-cache teardown. These were migration defects, separate from historical Phaser defects. The adaptive planner remains between fights and does not issue model calls inside the combat loop.

- Local evidence exists under ignored output/qa and source-tracked prototype notes/toolchain documents. This public audit records outcomes and source identities rather than reproducing raw private tool output.

## Provenance and licensing

Runtime art and original generation job identifiers are documented in ATTRIBUTION.md and assets/*/manifest.json, including pixel, combat-v3, royal-v4, gothic-v5 and godot-v6 revisions. Each historical asset event is listed below with its Git identity. Higgsfield originals were authorized by the user; paid fallback services were not inferred. Imported source packs retain their own licenses and attribution. No user music recording was copied from YouTube. The user explicitly selected closer licensed/original music after the recording-rights question.

The earlier Kevin MacLeod cues were CC BY and later replaced after the user rejected similar sounding cues. Twelve Scott Buckley CC BY themes separate menu, time passage, nine visitors and aftermath. Fifteen edited Chequered Ink sounds supply distinct impacts and equipment sounds. Source/license captures are provenance inventory, not agent-authored code. Ansimuz CC0 tiles informed the v5 hall. Quaternius motion was reference only for the Godot revision; Raven icons and Deep Fold pixel-planet work were visual references, not runtime imports unless a manifest states otherwise. Check the current ATTRIBUTION.md and resource manifests for the exact license URLs and edited-file lists.

## November 20 kinetic combat follow-up

The user requested an actual physical transformation, different phase-two move names and animation types, successive basic attacks with distinct combo slashes, more active independent enemy moves, smoother player movement, footsteps, immersive dialogue without counters, a crossed-sword/blast-back/stab opening and visibly coarse pixel sprites. This later request supersedes the earlier same-silhouette second stance.

Implementation: base combo rows are newly generated horizontal cut, rising backhand and overhead finisher. Quick repeated presses buffer two follow-ups; recoveries can chain. Hollow Sovereign uses a separate broken-crown/torn-mantle/cyan-fissure atlas and a six-frame transformation, with Gloam Rake, descending Crownfall blades, inward Royal Undertow and Last Dominion. Ground acceleration/braking, air control, jump buffering/coyote time and jump-release height replace immediate velocity changes. Ground-distance foot contacts sound for king and visitors; aerial motion does not tick footsteps. Nine mobility profiles add grounded rushes, vaults, armored charges and melee chains.

Presentation: four successful Higgsfield GPT Image2.6 jobs used the authorized unlimited2k/medium configuration. A batch accepted one job and explicitly rejected three429 requests without IDs; only those rejected items were submitted sequentially. Original results, full prompts, job IDs, hashes and processing scripts are preserved under assets/kinetic-v7. All four new atlases passed nonempty, clipping, binary-alpha and two-pixel-grid checks. Integer actor scale removes fractional smoothing. Existing actors, effects, coronation and held-finisher received matching cell-isolated pixel exports.

Validation: native court71 + game37 + planner28 =136 checks passed. The game tests now exercise buffered follow-ups, timed combo reset, acceleration, ground/air foot contacts, a proactive acrobat vault and dagger melee chains. Older movement and lunge tests were adapted to tick actual acceleration/player physics. One native audio teardown warning in the expanded fixture was resolved by waiting for deferred audio/resource release after freeing the game; the final build is clean. Final browser evidence and any remaining limitation are recorded in docs/kinetic-combat.md and ignored output/qa; historical captures are separately labeled.

The preceding Godot release5b73735 was published successfully and publicly verified as actual Godot4.7.2 WASM/PCK with zero game errors/warnings. This new revision is captured as working-tree source below; publication is not claimed before deployment verification.


## November 20 memory and poise follow-up

User direction: the anonymous cats must clearly become recognizable as the immortal king’s own earlier lives, with a meaningful name reveal and departing spirits before the final nova. Fix seated hovering and dialogue/weapon layering. Give both sides longer anticipation and recovery around fast contact, forbid player recovery cancellation, prevent permanent enemy hit-stun with damage-based armor breaks, and add satisfying timed guards/counters, individual shields and readable colored area warnings. The menu should be minimal, atmospheric and narratively separate from the arena.

Implementation: authored two-exchange dialogue now builds private memory clues toward Morrow and his own past lives retained in the crown. Lethal finales reclaim his name after the held physical stab, release nine actual accessory-specific translucent cat sprites, then finish with No more kings and the nova/ruined hall. Dialogue panels are fully opaque in CanvasLayer100 above world sprites. The seat uses885/384 with hips on the real cushion near348, rather than mistaking the lower platform for the cushion. New menu artwork depicts a discarded royal sword/crown on the road to a distant castle; small unboxed controls preserve its negative space.

Combat: per-life poise thresholds55/76/100/70/72/125/68/90/108 take real damage without cancelling an attack until a break. A0.48-second stagger and2.35-second post-break immunity prevent repeated reset. Guarding chips health and drains stamina; all damage routes including base thrust use the shared directional guard handler. Player anticipation can cancel through fresh guard, jump or dash, or be interrupted by damage; active/recovery commit. Longer recovery visibly holds follow-through before settling. Three-press combo inputs persist through the longer chain window. Perfect guard lasts0.12seconds after a fresh press, with0.34second rearm; it prevents damage and opens0.75seconds for a faster1.55x physical counter. A regression test found reactive dodge could incorrectly evade that parried counter; counter/parried/hurt states are excluded from reactive evasion. Holding guard no longer cancels the counter windup.

Art/audio: four Higgsfield unlimited2k/medium jobs created the seated king, narrative menu, eleven shield identities in66frames, and six finite colored telegraph types in36frames. All114 animated cells pass nonempty, hard-alpha and pixel-grid checks. Full prompts/job IDs/hashes are in assets/memory-v8. Edited licensed Chequered Ink Foley gives perfect guard and poise break separate clean sounds. One bounded original synthesized orchestral accent supplements the existing twelve licensed compositions; rising tension now swells the score rather than making danger quieter, while anticipation, dialogue and impact breaths leave space. The official Animation vs Math score page was checked; that non-CC recording is not distributed.

Validation: final native84court +49game +28planner =161 checks pass. Native regressions cover numeric poise, no stun timer extension, guard timing, real counter hit while guard stays held, anticipation cancellation versus committed recovery, fixed AoE target and dynamic score contrast. Archived140 TypeScript checks and typecheck pass after aligning the optional Worker role with Morrow’s own past lives. Browser evidence distinguishes ordinary ending routes from debug-selected mechanic scenes. The dedicated native-input suite verifies held guard is not perfect, timed guard/counter, knight shield/poise/retaliation, immutable floor mark while moving and final named-nine-spirit release. Preliminary telegraph checks were legitimately interrupted by tutorial damage; the harness now creates spacing by actual dash/jump instead of overriding state. Final local/public outcomes are in docs/memory-and-poise.md and ignored QA reports.

## November 20 physical body animation correction

The user reported that lowered ears read as a dog, preparation looked like a hologram of the move, combat felt sluggish and every character needed a base walk cycle. This correction supersedes the prior slow-windup target while preserving readable impacts, poise, perfect blocks and the memory ending.

The tired king retains short upright triangular feline ears and a compact muzzle; fatigue is expressed through eyes, head, shoulders and seated posture. New six-pose body preparation sheets show feet, hips, shoulders and weapon loading for the base and transformed king and for each visitor weapon. A separate gait sheet gives the two king forms and previous ruler actual walk/run frames; all nine visitors retain independent six-frame walk cycles.

A runtime bug advanced arriving enemy position without advancing its stride clock, freezing its first walking frame. Arrival now advances distance and ground contacts. Stationary approach/attack states choose idle or preparation rather than running in place. Every tell plays all six preparation poses; contact and recovery use separate attack rows. Melee/thrust projected attack graphics are removed. Area placement marks remain only as restrained flat marks on the floor.

Basic player timing is0.14second preparation,0.065contact,0.19recovery before combo adjustments, compared with0.20/0.085/0.28 previously. Enemy preparations/recoveries are also shorter. Counter preparation now uses the physical thrust pose, matching its contact animation. Ground spells retain a longer body windup than the basic sword, with explicit positioning marks.

New sprites, exact prompts, generation IDs, frame/foot geometry and hashes are recorded under assets/stance-v9. Native components verify cropped frame content rather than merely animation counters; browser checks separately inspect actual walk/preparation atlas regions during real movement/attack inputs. Final validated outcomes and source-freeze boundary are recorded in docs/body-animation.md. The line-level inventory below captures the actual final source and resource changes.

## Physical body animation public QA follow-up

The public standard native UI/combat suite passed on a0f8fd6. The first public body test passed frame/region checks but failed a fixed410ms walking-distance assertion during live combat. The failure had not recorded start/end coordinates, so a specific wall-versus-hit-versus-render-sampling cause is not claimed. The failed report/screenshots are preserved in ignored output/qa/body-animation-live-v9-fixed-window-failure.

The walk helper now supplies native-input travel room near a wall, records position/velocity/motion traces, and holds the original movement key until100px observed gait travel within1.4seconds. The original minimum50px, at least three distinct frame/region requirements and strict zero-console-error/warning assertions remain. No player position, health, timing or game state is overwritten. The public rerun passed with all six normal/transformed gait regions and physical body preparation. Only QA/documentation/audit changes follow this result; runtime source and art remain identical to the already tested release.
